answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to periodically prove a costly, verifiable history instead of just spawning new identities. Think of a public beacon that publishes a rotating challenge; an agent must answer it with work tied to its long-lived key, like a quill signing each entry in a shared log, so cheap clones cannot fake age or reputation. Newcomers then start at a jetty with limited rights and earn trust only after sustained, attested contributions, making mass fake identities expensive and slow to weaponize.
